medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Students who require a leave of absence must submit a formal request to the Dean of Student Affairs who reviews the merits of the request  and approves requests on a case-by-case basis.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Students are provided multiple opportunities to participate in the Durham and surrounding communities through organized student-led initiatives with the Durham Public School System, local multi-disciplinary clinics, the North Carolina Rural Student Health Coalition, AMSA, APAMSA, HMSA, LMSA, LGBTQ, and SNMA groups. Social and community outreach activities are organized through the Davison Council, the DukeMed Student government. Students participate as mentors in NIH-funded and RWJ-funded pipeline programs,  with the Durham community and its public school system(BOOST) which begin as early as the 3rd grade and extend into the final years of college (SMDEP, SROP).
medSchoolStudLife.setting: DukeMed is physically contiguous with the main campus of Duke University. Durham is one of three communities which comprise the Research Triangle Park, one of the nation's most prolific research centers and one rich in cultural, educational, and recreational opportunities. The cost of living for the Durham and surrounding communities (Raleigh and Chapel Hill) is less when compared to other metropolitan areas, with a variety of housing options, and numerous recreational and cultural opportunities easily that are accessible and affordable. The area boasts the largest concentration of persons with terminal degrees (MD, PhDs) per capita in the country. North Carolina provides multiple opportunities for recreational, collegiate, recreational, and professional sports venues that are affordable and easily accessible. Duke University and Durham are home to the internationally renown American Dance Festival each year.
medSchoolStudLife.housing:
Students choose from a number of affordable on- and off-campus housing units. Housing costs are extremely affordable and accessible to the School of Medicine, Average rent in the surrounding area is estimated at 
$1500 - $1900/m.  Multiple affordable housing units, e.g. condos, town homes, single-family homes, are available close to the medical school and hospitals. The median price for a single family home in the Durham area currently is ~$350,000.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems:
The Sexual and Gender Diversity Advisory Council (SAGDAC) is a multidisciplinary, cross-institution gathering of LGBTQ+ stakeholders who serve as a think tank and hub for LGBTQ+ initiatives at Duke. 

SAGDAC has representation from clinical specialties within the School of Medicine, across Duke Health entities, as well as other organizations such as the Office of Institutional Equity, DukeMed Pride, Nursing, the Duke Center for Sexual and Gender Diversity (CSGD) - University Campus, Duke Law School, and LGBTQ+ members of our community. Together, SAGDAC provides advanced consultation and leadership in developing innovative LGBTQ+ clinical services, research, and educational programs, while also facilitating community engagement, effective Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity (SO/GI) data collection, and connecting our community through the Duke Health OutList.   https://medschool.duke.edu/about-us/equity-diversity-inclusion/get-involved/sexual-and-gender-diversity-advisory-council
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: Duke University School of Medicine supports disabled students in MD programs through the Student Disability Access Office (SDAO), which coordinates reasonable accommodations in compliance with the ADA. The school provides tailored support for medical students, including accessible learning environments and specific resources for trainees.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: As a student enrolled at Duke University School of Medicine, you are invited to take part in university-sponsored and university-based opportunities. LE WELL is also working to bring some of the offerings to the medical campus for ease of access.  https://medschool.duke.edu/education/health-professions-education-programs/office-le-well/student-wellness-resources-support
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: Our institutional culture is built upon our history and values.  Our shared values—respect, trust, inclusion, discovery and excellence—are more than aspirations.  They are the beliefs and behaviors that we expect of ourselves and our colleagues.  These are the ideals that we must uphold in order to earn and maintain our reputation for quality and integrity, and to inspire confidence with each other, and the world which we both serve and rely on for our future viability.  Our values dictate our conduct and drive our culture.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Students must have access to reliable personal transportation, such as a personal vehicle, in order to travel to clinical training sites located outside of Durham for MD2 year. Public transportation is limited and you should be prepared to rely on alternate modes of transport such as Uber/Lyft or other personally-sourced modes of transportation. Please note that training at clinical sites in the community is a fundamental part of our curriculum in preparing you to care for patients and families.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: For all clinical interactions throughout the four years, business professional attire is required of all students. For classroom/laboratory encounters, causal dress is accepted.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: DukeMed's advising system is unique and provides longitudinal advising through the four years of medical school. Four academic faculty are responsible for meeting with students beginning in the first
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Duke med students begin patient interactions in MD year 1 in Internal Medicine, Pediatrics, General Surgery, Psychiatry. OB-GYN, Radiology, Neurology and one elective in the 2nd year of med school.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Lecture-based, case-based. small group, simulations, preceptored-clinical groups are used throughout the four years of the curriculum
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Multiple opportunities to participate in approved outreach (outreach clinics, partnerships with the public school system, community advocacy) are available throughout the four years of medical school.
medSchoolCurriculum.rankStudents: Students are not ranked at DUSOM
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Attendance for all lecture-format classes is encouraged but not mandatory. All instructional materials are made available through secured internet access to students.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The curriculum stimulates rapid expansion of medical knowledge. First-year students study basic science principles alongside the first of two-years' introduction to clinical medicine. The second year is the clinical clerkship year. The third and fourth years are elective including half basic science/half clinical coursework with opportunities for mentored research at Duke or other academic sites, including but not limited to the NIH, a large network of Globally located sites, other post-graduate programs, e.g. MPH, JD, MBA, MPP, MDiv, BME, masters and PhD in Global Health. Students may elect from a number of dual-degree programs which begin during the third year. The fourth year is an advanced clinical clerkship year to prepare for post-graduate study. The MST Program provides MD/PhD degrees over a six-to-seven-year period. It is expected that candidates for this combined degree plan will have careers in academic medicine.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Duke School of Medicine has created the Primary Care Leadership Track (PCLT) to train students to become primary care leaders. This project builds on a longstanding partnership between Duke and the Durham community to understand the causes of health disparities, create a strong research focus on community engagement, and learn how to redesign clinical programs to better serve patient needs at the individual and population level. Patient-centered learning is the essence of the Primary Care Leadership Track at Duke. Students will learn about medicine from the eyes of their patients. Students will learn about community health through the eyes of the Durham community. The PCLT is for students who want to make a difference in primary care, our health care system, and how we work together with our patients and our communities to improve health.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: The DukeMed curriculum is unique in that at least one required year of research is part of the four year curriculum requirements toward graduation. Students may choose from an extensive list of basic science and clinical research programs at Duke, at the NIH, HHMI labs, or labs at other peer institutions in this country or internationally-located labs, including the Duke Clinical Research Institute (DCRI), the country's largest clinical research enterprise in the country. Students may also choose laboratory experiences at other medical schools/centers throughout the country and internationally, the NIH, HHMI, etc. Many students chose to extend their year of research, for which there is support to do so. The research component of the MD/PhD program begins in the third year of medical school. Multiple opportunities for competitive funding to support dual degree programs,  e.g. MD/MPH, MD/JD, MD/MBA, MD/MPublic Policy, MD/MS in Biomedical Engineering, MD/Masters in Divinity, MD/Masters an
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: The curriculum is divided into blocks of months, Yr1, blocks of weeks during clinical rotations Yrs 2 and 4, and extended months/years during the third research/study abroad/dual degree year.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Medical student participation in community outreach/service is expected of all students.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Minimum 12 months required research  to complete third year of medical school.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Duke University Medical Center, Duke Children's Hospital and Health Center, Durham Regional Hospital, the Veteran's Administration Hospital, Duke Raleigh Hospitals, Lennox Baker Children's Hospital. I
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Pass-Fall for the first year basic science curriculum, Honors-Pass-Fail for the second, third and fourth years of the curriculum

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Advancing Health Together. As a world-class academic and health care system, Duke Health strives to transform medicine and health locally and globally through innovative scientific research, rapid translation of breakthrough discoveries, educating future clinical and scientific leaders, advocating and practicing evidence-based medicine to improve community health, and leading efforts to eliminate health inequalities.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: DukeMed is a diverse and inclusive community of trainees devoted to understanding the causes, prevention and treatment of human disease. These endeavors are embraced by all students committed to the highest academic goals utilizing unparalleled resources in education, clinical care, and research. Our objective is to educate physicians with our innovative curricula and broad-based clinical and research training.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: Each applicant must submit a minimum four (4) letters of recommendations.  We would prefer that the letters have a significant level of familiarity with the applicant, whether it is from the academic, research, clinical or community service environments.  Letters should not be a reiteration of academic achievements or course grades.   If your school submits a committee letter, this satisfies the four-letter rule. In other words, if you have a committee letter, you won't need to submit four letters of recommendation.  Letters should be on letterhead, dated and signed.  Letters must be received by the deadline of November 16th.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Applicants will interact virtually with members of the DukeMed Community at orientation and will participate in the Multiple Mini Interview (MMI).  Applicants will also meet and talk with current students about their experiences in the curriculum, living in Durham, their involvement in the school and community.
medSchoolApplication.regionalInterview: Regional interviews are no longer available
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: All AMCAS applicants who indicate Duke on their AMCAS application will receive a secondary application
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: We consider out of state applicants
medSchoolApplication.acceptInternationalApplInformation: We consider International Applicants with two years at an accredited US University or Canadian University
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo: Policies and updates will be made to the Duke School of Medicine Admissions website at https://medschool.duke.edu/education/health-professions-education-programs/doctor-medicine-md-program/office-md-admissions
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: We consider the highest score from one specific test.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Any courses that are taken at community colleges and accepted at your undergraduate institution will also be accepted.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Applicants are welcome to send letters of intent, letters of interest and significant updates and achievements.  These documents will become a permanent part of the application.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: The study of medical sciences is not a pure intellectual exercise. Candidates for all degree programs within the School of Medicine (SOM) must possess the ability to learn, integrate, analyze, and synthesize data. This document is a general guidance document; individual programs may have more rigorous motor, sensory, or other requirements in their individual technical standards. In general students should have certain minimum physical, emotional, cognitive and social capacities to complete all requirements of their individual school either directly or through reasonable accommodations.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: The Office of Financial Aid requires the Need Access, FAFSA, parent and student tax returns. Students applying for only Federal Loans complete the FAFSA. Students are encouraged to submit the applications as soon as possible after acceptance. Prior year tax returns should be submitted. 89% of currently enrolled medical students receive some type of financial aid. Several full and partial (Dean's) Tuition Scholarships are awarded to students who based on proven academic excellence and backgrounds that will contribute to the diversity of the class. Students who enter the Medical Scientist Training Program receive full tuition, fees, and a stipend.
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: Students are required to pay four years of medical tuition. If a student attends a dual degree program, tuition will be charged for both programs. There are no additional tuition charges for Continuation of Research, remediation or retaking of a failed course.

medSchoolPrograms.name: Summer Medical and Dental Education Program (SMDEP)

Duke University Summer Research Opportunity Program (SROP) is a ten-week training program designed to give motivated undergraduate students hands-on experience in graduate-level biomedical research leading to careers  at the MD/PhD and PhD level.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Wait-listed applicants will be notified initially by phone from the Associate Dean of Admissions on behalf of the Committee on Admissions.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: Duke University School of Medicine encourages broad-based interdisciplinary academic preparation in the sciences and humanities. Our academic expectations include multidisciplinary coursework in the biomedical sciences, comprehension of the analysis of research data, understanding of the interconnections of basic science and clinical medicine, familiarity with patient needs in healthcare, and knowledge of the biological basis of behavior. Expository writing is a fundamental expectation in the preparation for medicine.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: Students should have completed any expected degrees, postbac work no earlier than 5 years prior to application
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: DukeMed’s evaluation is based on a number of critical elements which include experiences and academics.  Applicants must have the following: worked or volunteered in patient focused venues, demonstrated a desire to care for all, leadership capabilities, team building competence, excellent written and communication skills, supportive letters of recommendation and participation in scholarly experience.   The invitation only Multi Mini Interview (MMI) will be another component of this assessment.  Duke University does not discriminate on the basis of age, color, disability, gender, gender expression, gender identity, genetic information, national origin, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, or veteran status.
